record_type_quote: To determine the viability of Gould’s criticism of the Army Beta time limits and his claim that the Army Beta could not measure intelligence, we replicated his administration of the test to a sample of undergraduate students.

targets.title: The Mismeasure of Man.
targets.evidence_quote: To determine the viability of Gould’s criticism of the Army Beta time limits and his claim that the Army Beta could not measure intelligence, we replicated his administration of the test to a sample of undergraduate students.
targets.outcome_quote: Given these results from our replication, it seems that Gould’s criticism of time limits and his argument that the Army Beta did not measure intelligence are without basis.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The overall verdict rejects Gould’s substantive claims about time limits and validity. Some completion rates match and the administration appears honest, but the authors’ overall judgment is that his central criticisms are without basis. The cited 1981 edition, not the later revised edition, is the target.

targets.title: Psychological Examining in the United States Army.
targets.evidence_quote: To further test the viability of the one-factor model, we performed confirmatory factor analysis on two correlation matrices of Army Beta data for World War I draftees ([15], pp. 390, 634).
targets.outcome_computational_quote: To further test the viability of the one-factor model, we performed confirmatory factor analysis on two correlation matrices of Army Beta data for World War I draftees ([15], pp. 390, 634).
targets.outcome_robustness_quote: Thus, even in two samples of World War I draftees—groups that would be much more likely to have a separate factor for recognition of written numbers than a modern sample of college students—a one-factor model fit the data just as well as a two-factor model. Again, parsimony dictates that researchers should favor a one-factor model of intelligence from the historic Army Beta data.
targets.outcome_reasoning: A secondary reproduction reanalyses two original correlation matrices using alternative factor models to test the substantive validity finding. Recovering original reported coefficients was outside this analysis; the original general-ability interpretation survives the tested alternative. Both matrices belong to one original volume.

reasoning: Primary empirical component collects new undergraduate data to retest Gould’s published administration and claims, so record_type is replication. A secondary original-data factor reanalysis of Yerkes’s 1921 matrices is coded with reproduction axes at its own target. Historical materials, critiques of other chapters, and other test-development books are not additional targets. Article title and all four authors verified in full-text header.
